positions.sentence: Policies warn that AI tools may store, reuse or train on what users enter, so entered information may not stay private.
Policies state that university-approved or licensed AI tools protect entered data and do not use it to train models.
Policies warn that entering sensitive data into AI tools can violate FERPA, HIPAA or other privacy rules and expose institutional or student data.
Users must not enter confidential, sensitive, personally identifiable or restricted data into AI tools.
Users must not enter sensitive or confidential data into public, consumer or unapproved AI tools unless the tool is approved for that data.
Sensitive or confidential university data may be used only with AI tools that the university has approved, licensed or contractually protected.
Public data may be used freely with AI tools.
Users should avoid entering sensitive, personal or confidential information into AI tools.
Users should enter only public information into AI tools and assume anything entered becomes public.
Users should minimize, anonymize or de-identify data before entering it into AI tools.
Users should check the data's classification and consult the data owner or IT before entering non-public data into AI tools.
Users must protect data and privacy and follow university data and privacy policies and laws when using AI.
Students must not enter personal, confidential or sensitive information into AI tools.
Instructors must not enter student work or identifiable student information into AI tools without student consent or without approved tools.
Instructors should not upload student work to AI detection tools, which may expose student data.
Instructors should tell students about AI data privacy risks, for example in the syllabus.
Instructors must not require students to enter personal information or original work into AI tools.
The university must vet AI tools and put data protection measures in place.
Users should opt out of data training, adjust privacy settings and read privacy policies before using AI tools.
Researchers and staff must not enter unpublished research, intellectual property or proprietary material into AI tools.
